mutants.targets-nfr: exactly-once transfers require microbatch topology
mutants.wrong-design: Deposits and transfers are processed in a stream topology (non-idempotent +sum / balance debit under retry) instead of a microbatch topology.

mutants.targets-nfr: unbounded transfer history must be subindexed (iterator reads)
mutants.wrong-design: Incoming/outgoing transfer histories are plain nested maps (no :subindex?), so each history read loads the whole unbounded collection as one value.

mutants.targets-nfr: heartbeats perform no durable writes (presence is ephemeral)
mutants.wrong-design: Each heartbeat is appended to a depot and a stream topology writes a durable last-beat PState that presence reads.

killed-by.context: chat-app: durable write volume of hot writes heartbeats perform no durable writes
chat-app: durable state survives module update; presence resets presence resets on restart; next heartbeat revives it

mutants.targets-nfr: a room post must not write per room member (bounded write amplification)
mutants.wrong-design: Every room message is also fanned out into a per-member inbox PState, so a post to an N-member room does N extra writes.

mutants.targets-nfr: edit and version-read cost independent of history length
mutants.wrong-design: Inlines the upstream module but declares the per-document $$edits log as a plain (non-subindexed) vector, so every edit and every doc+version read loads and rewrites the whole history.

mutants.targets-nfr: document read cost independent of history length
mutants.wrong-design: Drops the materialized $$docs PState and has the doc+version query replay the entire edit log from the empty string on every read.

mutants.targets-nfr: horizontal scalability: campaigns partitioned across tasks
mutants.wrong-design: Declares $$campaigns with {:global? true} and routes both the microbatch ingest and the windows-in-range query to |global, so all campaigns live on a single task.

mutants.targets-nfr: query cost independent of click volume (pre-aggregated windows)
mutants.wrong-design: Stores each counted click as a raw [geo device delta] row keyed by request-id under the window instead of +compound totals/breakdown counters, and folds all raw rows of each window into totals and breakdown at query time.

mutants.targets-nfr: flag read is a point lookup independent of flags per environment
mutants.wrong-design: Partitions and keys flags by (tenant, env) with a subindexed flag-key map per environment, and flag reads fetch every flag of the environment via foreign-select ALL and linearly scan for the requested key.

mutants.targets-nfr: horizontal scalability: flags partitioned across tasks
mutants.wrong-design: Declares $$flags with {:global? true} and adds |global to the microbatch so every flag write and read goes to a single task.

mutants.targets-nfr: README:272 a file's whole version history must not be used as one value
mutants.wrong-design: A file's :versions map is not subindexed, so every commit and version read loads and rewrites the file's whole version history as one value.

mutants.targets-nfr: README:257-275 cancel-booking! proportional to stay nights; availability must not be recomputed by scanning bookings
mutants.wrong-design: cancel-booking! reads every booking of the property and recomputes each stay night's availability as capacity minus confirmed quantities.

mutants.targets-nfr: bounded storage: expired raw samples and rollup buckets are deleted
mutants.wrong-design: Clock advancement only writes the new clock and removes all three expiry branches, so expired raw samples, 60s buckets, and 3600s buckets are never deleted.

mutants.targets-nfr: per-sample write and range-read cost independent of bucket count
mutants.wrong-design: Makes the per-series 60s bucket map non-subindexed, so each sample, expiry pass, and range query reads the whole map and (for writes) rewrites it via termval instead of using +compound and sorted-map-range.

mutants.targets-nfr: README resource guarantees: no unbounded per-tenant collection (journal) read/deserialized/rewritten as one value; get-journal proportional to limit
mutants.wrong-design: The tenant's journal is stored as one non-subindexed sorted-map value: every fund!/charge!/refund! reads, deserializes and rewrites the whole journal, and get-journal fetches the whole journal and pages it client-side.

mutants.targets-nfr: README:36,47-50 atomic two-bucket debit and idempotent decisions under engine retry
mutants.wrong-design: Checks run in a stream topology, so a retried check between the debit and the decision write can debit twice.

mutants.targets-nfr: top-k query cost proportional to k, not to candidates per prefix
mutants.wrong-design: Reads every ranked candidate of the prefix with subselect ALL and takes the top k in the query instead of a bounded sorted-set-range-from-start of k.

mutants.targets-nfr: load spread within a locale (no hot partition per locale)
mutants.wrong-design: Changes the partition key from [locale, first two chars of the phrase/prefix] to [locale] alone, placing a locale's entire corpus and query load on one task.

mutants.targets-nfr: README :258 'the book of a symbol must not be held as a single value read and rewritten whole on every command'; get-depth proportional to levels
mutants.wrong-design: Each side's price levels and per-level FIFO queues are stored as one non-subindexed map value per symbol, so every submit/cancel reads and rewrites the whole side of the book and get-depth fetches the whole side and sorts it client-side.

mutants.targets-nfr: hold cost proportional to requested seats, not to total holds on the event
mutants.wrong-design: For HoldSeats commands, rebuilds the requested seats' occupancy by selecting and scanning every hold of the event (seats-from-holds) instead of trusting the per-seat records passed to decide.

mutants.targets-nfr: exactly-once click counting under retries/concurrency
mutants.wrong-design: Switches the core topology from microbatch to stream and moves click dedup to a client-side check-then-append (foreign-select on :click-ids before append), so the topology increments clicks unconditionally and retries or concurrent duplicate clicks double-count.

mutants.targets-nfr: README:18 get-stats-for-range efficient for ranges up to multiple years
mutants.wrong-design: Only minute/hour/day rollups are kept (no 30-day level), so a multi-year range reads ~1 day bucket per day of range.

mutants.targets-nfr: exactly-once aggregate ingestion (microbatch)
mutants.wrong-design: Ingestion runs in a stream topology, so +combine aggregates can double-count under retry.
